<reason>PRO sustained the key distinction between limiting and abolishing bans, with sunsets, notice, and retrospective review answering sovereignty and emergency concerns. CON repeatedly asserted desperate governments would breach, but never supplied a cross-border check on pre-emptive or prolonged bans. PRO also showed enforceable limits can deter cascades and shorten bans even without perfect compliance.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: automatic expiry operates before any tribunal ruling, and CON's domestic-accountability check rewards banning because harmed neighbours cannot vote the banning government out.</best_rebuttal>
